reviewContext: President-authorized transition from a machine-readable law registry to explicit self-describing organ contracts plus deterministic transitive dependency compilation, together with bounded Lyapunov stability and exact-for-declared-finite-model viability primitives; the new SAFE_CONTROL capability restricts optimization to declared viable states/actions where requested and preserves the distinction between sampled evidence, exact finite-model certificates and claims about continuous or unmodeled reality
reviewedSemantics: SETKA_MACHINE_KERNEL_V1 now contains an explicit organRegistry; every declared ship organ must expose organId, version, purpose, inputs, outputs, lawReferences, dependencies, invariants, materializationPolicy, resourceMetrics, provenanceRequirements and failClosedRules before it counts as kernel self-knowledge

the compiler validates machine-kernel self-knowledge before building and fails closed if an organ contract is incomplete, references an unknown law, depends on an unknown organ, or is referenced by a capability without a declared organ contract

capability tokens are no longer incorrectly emitted as ship organs; requested capabilities expand to declared organ IDs and the compiler resolves the complete transitive dependency closure deterministically

compiled blueprint organ entries now reference their versioned machine-kernel contract using SETKA_MACHINE_KERNEL_V1#organRegistry.<ORGAN_ID>; the blueprint references laws and contracts instead of copying the whole kernel into each ship

the current organ registry covers base identity, causal memory, replay, provenance, runtime safety and self-diagnostic organs together with generative geometry, fold/unfold, bifurcation scaling, branching/shared prefix, Least Verified Action, attractor analysis, adaptive evidence budgeting, local refinement, scale analysis, computational irreducibility, privacy/hierarchical memory and safe-control organs

LYAPUNOV_STABILITY is implemented with a positive quadratic V over a declared equilibrium and discrete delta V=V(next)-V(current); an increasing V or departure from equilibrium rejects the stability candidate
nonexhaustive Lyapunov transitions produce SAMPLED_STABILITY_EVIDENCE only; they never prove global stability

an exact Lyapunov certificate is permitted only for an explicitly declared exhaustive finite model whose transition count matches the declared finite domain and whose non-equilibrium transitions strictly decrease V while equilibrium is preserved; the result explicitly disclaims a universal physical-system claim

FINITE_VIABILITY_KERNEL computes the greatest controlled-invariant fixed point of a complete declared finite deterministic state/action transition model by repeatedly removing safe states with no allowed action returning to the current candidate kernel

finite viability computation fails closed on missing transitions, actions pointing outside the declared state model or an unresolved fixed point; exactness is limited to the declared finite model and never promoted to a continuous/unmodeled-world guarantee

SAFE_CONTROL is now a compilable capability containing LYAPUNOV_STABILITY and FINITE_VIABILITY_KERNEL plus their base safety, diagnostic and provenance dependencies; a complete normalized intent compiles this without AI reading the kernel

the safe-control policy states that when the capability is required the system first restricts candidate actions to the declared viability kernel, then evaluates stability evidence, and only then allows Least Verified Action to compare resource cost; a cheaper nonviable action is not a valid optimization candidate

Kernel Map registers stability_control as CRITICAL, routes core/safety and tests/setka-stability-viability.test.mjs through a dedicated STABILITY_VIABILITY check group, and adds self-knowledge/dependency-closure review targets to ship_compiler

Kernel Pulse review run 33769478867 executed syntax checks for changed executables, Generative Geometry 14/14, Least Verified Action/scaling/adaptive-budget 15/15, Ship Kernel Compiler 11/11, Stability/Viability 7/7, Kernel Handshake 8 cases and Mission Gate 20 cases; all executable tests passed and unclassified executable count was zero

the MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED result of run 33769478867 was the expected governance response to a new CRITICAL stability_control component, two new protected files and protected ship-compiler/kernel-governance semantic drift; it was not a test failure

this transition does not implement a continuous-state viability solver, a symbolic/global Lyapunov theorem prover, a control-barrier-function solver, an autonomous production autopilot, an autonomous natural-language parser, or self-accepted kernel-law mutation

no PostgreSQL schema, Supabase writer, Edge Function, production fleet runtime, canonical transcript row or cryosleep state was modified; all recovery, backup, handshake, authority and transcript-readback gates remain authoritative
